messages:
Maria Chen: Quick question — for cross-org model routing (customer A -> model pool in proj B), do we want callers to hand off their original API key to the routing layer, or should the router mint short-lived service tokens?
Devin Patel: my vote: mint ephemeral tokens. handing original API keys around sounds risky and breaks scoping/audit.
Ryan O'Leary: +1 to short-lived. also helps with rotation and limited audience. but we need to think about traceability — how do we link eventual model usage back to the original actor?
Claire: could add an immutable `caller_claim` on the ephemeral token that the router signs (not replacing the original), then backends log both token id and caller_claim. minimal perf hit. :thinking:
Devin Patel: example claim sketch:
```json
{
  "iss": "auth-router",
  "sub": "svc-router-01",
  "aud": "model-serving:pool-xyz",
  "claims": {
    "original_api_key_id": "ak_12345",
    "original_org": "org-foo",
    "original_user": "user:bob@example.com",
    "scopes": ["generate:text","embed:create"]
  },
  "exp": 1699999999
}
```
Maria Chen: that looks good. important tradeoffs:
- short-lived tokens reduce blast radius and make rotation simpler.
- router-signed claims mean we must trust the router and its KMS; increases trust surface.
- we need RBAC mapping when model pool enforces org/project boundaries (e.g., some pools only serve certain tenants).
Ryan O'Leary: on RBAC mapping: two layers — router enforces pre-checks (deny early), model-serving enforces post-checks (defense in depth). router should fail-fast for org mismatches.
Claire: how do we handle delegated service actors (svc A acts on behalf of svc B)? Do we allow chaining claims? Could be abused.
Devin Patel: propose single-level delegation only. If svcA needs to act for svcB, router produces an ephemeral token with `delegated_from` claim and short TTL. No deep nesting.
Maria Chen: logging & audit: store original_api_key_id in immutable logs + append router token id. This lets billing + security correlate. Also include `route_path` to reconstruct how many hops.
auth-bot: New policy created: `svc-ephemeral-default` — TTL 5m, aud-limited, requires `original_api_key_id` present.
Ryan O'Leary: perf note — minting per-request could add latency. mitigate with a tiny cache keyed by (original_api_key_id, pool, scopes) for 1m. still rotate when backend indicates revocation.
Claire: migration plan idea:
1) enable router in `opt-in` mode (it mirrors but doesn't reject).
2) start emitting router-signed ephemeral tokens in headers (X-Redwood-Ephemeral) while continuing accept original API keys.
3) after 30d telemetry + audits, flip to reject un-ephemeral requests for cross-org routes.
Devin Patel: SDK changes: add transparent router integration so apps get ephemeral header automatically. make it toggleable via env var.
Maria Chen: next steps: write short RFC with claim schema, RBAC mapping table, and migration schedule. assign owners: @Devin to draft claims + proxy KMS plan, @Claire to draft RBAC rules and deny-list, @Ryan to run perf sims.
Ryan O'Leary: ack, will simulate latency and cache hit distribution.
Devin Patel: will start RFC draft today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
